claim: For the Yang–Chen flow \(\dot x=a(y-x)\), \(\dot y=x(c-z)\), \(\dot z=xy-bz\) with \(a,b,c>0\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(\int x^2\,d\mu=b\bar z\), \(\int z^2\,d\mu=c\bar z\), and \(\operatorname{Var}_\mu(z)=\bar z(c-\bar z)\), where \(\bar z=\int z\,d\mu\). Thus \(0\le\bar z\le c\); the lower endpoint is only the origin measure and the upper endpoint is supported on the two outer equilibria. Consequently every non-equilibrium ergodic compact invariant measure has \(0<\bar z<c\), \(\int x^2\,d\mu<bc\), positive height variance, and positive mass both in \(0<z<c\) and in \(z<0\) or \(z>c\). In particular, any nonconstant periodic orbit with \(z(t)>0\) for all \(t\) visits both \(0<z<c\) and \(z>c\).

correctness.rationale: For compact invariant support, invariant averaging of the Lie derivatives of \(x^2/2\), \(z\), \(y^2/2\), and \(z^2/2\) gives \(\int xy=\int x^2=b\bar z\) and \(c\int xy=\int xyz=b\int z^2\), hence \(\int z^2=c\bar z\) and the variance parabola. Endpoint support geometry is checked directly from the vector field. A packaged symbolic verifier independently replays the algebra and returns VERIFY_OK. The proof makes no finite-time-to-infinite-time inference.

value.rationale: The result gives a finite-amplitude, exact global constraint on every compact recurrent statistical state of a classical unusual Lorenz-type flow. It ties mean height, height variance, and horizontal RMS to the equilibrium height \(c\), forces non-equilibrium recurrence to cross the equilibrium slab, and supplies a parameter-exact diagnostic for periodic or chaotic computations. This is structurally stronger than a local stability calculation or a numerical attractor statistic.
